clue.text: Support when one's getting into carriage

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: something getting into a thing goes inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: carriage is the way one holds oneself, one's stance or posture
one is I, and one's is I'S, written IS

explanation.surface: A helping hand offered as someone climbs into a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a coach, but here it means bearing or posture.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance is help or backing, a straightforward synonym of support as a noun.

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth
ca. is the abbreviation of circa, about

explanation.surface: A queen has come to a harbour town that has been worn out and exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: ER followed by CA, written upwards, reads ACRE. 'Used' only joins the wordplay to the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre (Akko) is an ancient harbour city in northern Israel, so it is an example of a port.

clue.text: Allows move capturing knight on board

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: being on board means being inside a steamship, SS, whose two letters go either side
a move is an action taken
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A chess player permits a move that captures a knight on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess makes 'on board' read as the chessboard, but it is the ship whose two letters go round everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction something is to authorise or permit it, so sanctions is a synonym of allows.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a young castrated bull, one of the herd
second meaning: to guide or direct, as you drive a car

explanation.surface: A beast that is part of a cattle drive across the range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cattle drive' reads as one cowboy phrase, but the split comes between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A steer is a bullock raised for beef, and to steer is to guide a vehicle or herd in a direction.

clue.text: Sheepish like bad actor ended gutted

indicators.note: a gutted fish has had its insides removed, so only the outer letters of the word stay

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a ham is an overacting, poor performer
only the first and last letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: An actor who gave a dreadful performance feels sheepish and gutted when the show closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' looks like British slang for very disappointed, which suits the surface, but it strips the middle out of 'ended'.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sheepish is feeling embarrassed by what one has done, the same as being ashamed.

clue.text: Decay covering tail of polar bears

indicators.note: a thing covering another wraps round it, so one piece sits around another

parts.note: caries is the decay of teeth or bone

indicators.note: the tail is the end, so only the last letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of polar

explanation.surface: Rot spreading over the tails of polar bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polar bears' reads as the animal, but bears is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry a load is to bear it, so carries is a synonym of bears.

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A gardener now and then uses a hoe to dig up grubs from around a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A herb is a small non-woody plant, often one used in cooking, so it is a kind of plant.

indicators.note: a shaved head has lost its top, so the word's first letter goes

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier keeping guard

explanation.surface: A skinhead bouncer controls access to a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry is the right or means of getting in, a direct synonym of access as a noun.

clue.text: Growing desire maybe stiffening corset suppresses

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold something in, so one piece is kept inside another

parts.note: boning is the strips of stiffening material sewn into a corset
an urge is one kind of desire

explanation.surface: A tightly laced corset holds back a swelling longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiffening' reads as a verb but is the noun for corset reinforcement.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgeoning means flourishing or expanding quickly, so it is a synonym of growing.

clue.text: What holds quick thinker Descartes back?

parts.note: fast means quick

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the name is read from its end

parts.note: René Descartes was the French philosopher

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what restrains a rapid-minded philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cryptic 'What holds', a thing that holds something closed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastener is a clip, button or catch, a device whose job is to keep things held together.

parts.note: a candidate runs for office, so was a candidate is ran

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what say means in 'fruit, say'

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone stood for election to show that the ticket was diverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a wide variety of things, as in a range of options, so it can mean diversity.

clue.text: The man, Beam, embracing sweetheart? Paradise!

parts.note: the man is referred to as he

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a rafter is a sloping roof beam

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so the centre letter of sweet is wanted

parts.note: the middle letter of sweet

explanation.surface: A man cuddling the setter Beam, his darling, is in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: Beam is the setter's own name, so it reads as a self-reference, but here it is a wooden beam. E goes after the first letter of RAFTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The hereafter is the life after death, the heaven or paradise believers expect.

indicators.note: to surround something is to enclose it on all sides, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: to pound is to beat heavily, to throb
m is the symbol for mass
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Blood clots in a heart that beats alone around a growth.
explanation.walkthrough: THROB goes around M, and I is added after, although the clue names single before the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrombi is the plural of thrombus, the medical name for a blood clot formed in a vessel.

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so the word is chosen for how it is spoken

parts.note: a season is a time of year

explanation.surface: Cooking advice: season thoroughly when given a herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly season' reads as season thoroughly; soundly is really the sound-alike signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic herb used to flavour food, so it is an example of a seasoning.

clue.text: Honourable guy holding current Republican up

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a guy is a rope or cable holding a tent or mast steady

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: An upright man supporting the present Republican administration.
explanation.walkthrough: A guy is the rope or wire that steadies a tent or mast, not a man here.
explanation.definitionFit: Creditable means deserving praise or respect, which is close to honourable in describing conduct.

indicators.note: gripping something means holding it tightly within, so one piece is inside another

parts.note: rooted to the spot means firmly fixed
S is the south pole

explanation.surface: A bird came to rest, clinging firmly to a perch.
explanation.walkthrough: The pole looks like the bird's perch, but it is a magnetic pole, south.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird that roosted settled down on a perch for the night, so roosted means settled.

indicators.note: circling something means going all the way around it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: current affairs are topical ones
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A hot ocean current swirling around a river mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as a flow of water beside 'river', but it means up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical weather is very hot, and boiling is informal for extremely hot, so the words match.

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A sprite who is a little naughty and controlling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sandman is a folklore figure who sprinkles sand to bring sleep, a fairy-tale being.

clue.text: Noisome gas to release around outlet?

indicators.note: the answer lies around in the words, scattered in plain view across them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the last

explanation.surface: A foul gas is let out from an outlet vent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlet' suggests a vent for gas; the question mark flags its retail sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastore is a very large shop, and a retail outlet is a shop, so it is an example.

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector, so detective's is DI'S
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A detective has gone off to investigate a crime spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caper' looks like a noun for a heist, but it is the verb, to frolic.
explanation.definitionFit: To disport oneself is to play or frolic, and to caper is to skip about playfully.

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: the last letter of agent
to bug someone is to annoy them

explanation.surface: A spy in the end plants bugs in loudspeakers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tannoy is a British brand name used generally for a public-address system.
explanation.definitionFit: Tannoys are public-address loudspeaker systems, as used for station announcements, so they are speaker systems.

clue.text: Round figure gone, finally fashion model

parts.note: par is the expected score for a round of golf
ago means gone by, in the past

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so just the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the last letter of fashion

explanation.surface: A fashion model whose curvy figure has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round figure' suggests a curvy shape or zero, but it is the golf score for a round.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example to be imitated, the same as a model of virtue.

clue.text: Papers over item oddly for gift

parts.note: the press is the newspapers collectively

indicators.note: oddly means in the odd positions, so the first and third letters are kept

parts.note: the first and third letters

explanation.surface: Newspaper wrapped around an odd item to make a present.
explanation.walkthrough: Pressie is informal British for a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressie is a colloquial word for a present, which is a gift.

indicators.note: overturning something turns it upside down, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: is means exists, lives
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Someone sharing a house with a rat that knocks over the bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsi is the plural of tarsus, the group of bones in the ankle, so they are bones.

clue.text: Repeat episodes, resembling UKTV network principally?

definitions.text: Repeat episodes, resembling UKTV network principally?

indicators.note: principally means first of all, so the first letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A dig that a British TV network mostly shows repeats.
explanation.walkthrough: UKTV runs British channels such as Dave and Gold that show many old programmes again, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a repeat broadcast of a programme, which is what a channel full of repeated episodes shows.

indicators.note: to finish off here is to take off the finish, the last letter of the word

parts.note: something unwanted is needless, unnecessary

explanation.surface: An order to complete unnecessary drains.
explanation.walkthrough: Sewers reads as drains, but the question mark points to things that sew.
explanation.definitionFit: Needles are the tools that sew stitches, so in the punning sense they are sewers.

clue.text: Problems possibly getting mouth round sibilant

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: the lips form the mouth
S is a sibilant, hissing consonant

explanation.surface: Trouble wrapping one's mouth around a hissing sound.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface describes exactly the speech problem that is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisps are speech defects, so they are possibly problems someone has in talking.

indicators.note: being in something means being placed inside it, so one letter goes within the word

parts.note: a flutter is British slang for a small bet
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Something left in a flurry of activity when a strip was seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt is a long narrow band, as in a belt of land, so it is a strip.

clue.text: Primitive arrow part by incomplete fire

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing a part, here its final letter

parts.note: a barb is the backward-pointing point of an arrowhead
to fire someone up is to arouse them

explanation.surface: Early weapons: part of an arrow beside a fire that never quite got going.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarous means uncivilised or savage, which overlaps with primitive in the sense of crude and rough.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: took, pinched, as a thief does
second meaning: a long scarf or wrap worn over a woman's dress

explanation.walkthrough: The surface shows a lady raising her dress; lifted means pinched. A stole is worn with a gown rather than being one, a loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Stole is the past tense of steal, and a stole is a woman's shawl worn over the shoulders.

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is chosen for how it is spoken

parts.note: to take home pay is to earn it

explanation.surface: Reports that someone carries a bird back to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Take home looks like carrying something home, but here it is take-home pay.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a bird beloved of crossword setters.

clue.text: Review of idiots married in broadcast

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: being in something means being placed inside it, so one letter goes within the word

parts.note: to broadcast a message is to send it out, sent
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A critic's write-up of a TV show about married fools.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is an evaluation or appraisal, which is what a review provides.
